scientific_hypothesis: Partitioning 28 layers into 14 contiguous HfO2/SiO2 bilayer units and initializing each unit around nominal quarter-wave optical thicknesses (±15% tolerance) with a soft penalty on inter-layer thickness jumps >40% will increase the fraction of physically valid candidates and improve best_target_score compared to purely randomized initialization, while preserving global non-periodicity across the stack.
expected_advantages: Higher valid_candidates count due to physically reasonable initialization
Improved best_target_score from better search space coverage
Reduced numerical_convergence failures compared to route_03
known_risks: May converge to local optimum near quarter-wave design rather than globally optimal non-quarter-wave solution
Thickness-jump penalty may overly constrain optimizer if penalty weight is too high
expected_observations: valid_candidates should be >= 15 if reduced layer count eases constraint satisfaction
best_target_score should remain >= 0.45 if 20 layers suffice for dual-band operation
total thickness should decrease compared to route_02 if fewer layers reduce cumulative thickness
If best_target_score drops below 0.40, hypothesis that 20 layers maintain acceptable performance is falsified
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improvement relative to historical best is < 1e-3 for 2 consecutive rounds, judge search as stagnated -> stop and retain current best
If valid_candidates = 0, judge constraint set infeasible -> should relax thickness bounds or increase layer count
If best_target_score < 0.40 consistently across 3 rounds, judge 20-layer topology insufficient -> should increase to 24 or 28 layers
